name: configuration
source: OpenAEV-Platform/openaev@cde7bee (openaev-api/src/main/resources/application.properties, the @Value and @ConfigurationProperties of the Java code)
intro: Every key OpenAEV reads at startup, from `application.properties` and from its code, grouped by block, with its environment variable: the key in upper case with each dot replaced by an underscore (`openaev.base-url` is `OPENAEV_BASE-URL`). **Shipped** says whether `application.properties` sets the key, shows it commented out, or leaves it to the code. A key also read under the former name `openbas.*` keeps that name working.

cells: Endpoint URL. Required when AI is enabled
Model to be used for text generation (depending on type)
Model to be used for image generation (depending on type)
Other spelling of `ai.model_images`, bound to the same setting; the platform reads it but no feature uses it.
Maximum number of expired expectations the Expectations Expiration Manager concludes in one run for each tenant; the rest waits for the next run. Default `1000`.

Turns on the Expectations Expiration Manager, the built-in job that concludes the pending expectations whose expiration time has passed (as failed, or as not vulnerable for a vulnerability expectation). When `false`, the job is never scheduled and expired expectations stay pending. Default `true`.

The platform reads it but only writes it in a debug log line; each expectation expires after its own expiration time, set on the inject or by default by the `openaev.expectation.<type>.expiration-time` keys. Unit: seconds, default `21600`.

The platform reads it but only writes it in a debug log line; each expectation expires after its own expiration time, set on the inject or by default by the `openaev.expectation.<type>.expiration-time` keys. Unit: seconds, default `3600`.

ID under which OpenAEV registers the built-in Expectations Expiration Manager collector and records its expiration results. The score computation recognizes these results by the default ID `96e476e0-b9c4-4660-869c-98585adf754d`, so keep the default.
Time in seconds between two runs of the Expectations Expiration Manager; the first run starts 30 seconds after startup. Default `60`.
Leave to `auto` or set `opensearch`: AWS SigV4 authentication only works with the OpenSearch client
Engine client timeouts and connection cap (defaults: 5s connect, 60s socket, 40 connections).
URL of the OpenSearch database, no http(s) prefix
Whether to use AWS SigV4 authentication Amazon OpenSearch or Amazon OpenSearch Serverless (`es` or `aoss`)
Prefix of the index and lifecycle policy names
Suffix appended to the name of the first index OpenAEV creates for each model behind its `<prefix>_<model>` alias, so that rollovers number the next ones; default `-000001`.
Maximum number of records fetched per indexing batch from the database

Indexing cursor grace window in seconds. The cursor persisted after each indexing round never gets closer to wall-clock than this window, so rows committed late by long write transactions are still indexed. Must exceed the longest expected write transaction.

How many models may run their indexing sync concurrently (default 3). Each sync pass holds a database connection for its whole fetch query; during a full reindex those queries are heavy, so a higher value trades platform responsiveness for reindexing throughput.
Threshold in milliseconds after which a model synchronisation is declared misfired and is rescheduled.

Delay in seconds after which the instance that applied an upgrade re-feeding an index in place (for example the findings index, to mask the sensitive values indexed before) re-feeds it a second time. During a rolling deploy, instances still running the previous version take part in the first re-feed and write their own documents, such as finding values in cleartext; the second re-feed rewrites them. Set it longer than your longest rolling deploy plus one indexing round (15 seconds). Set to `0` to skip the second re-feed, which is safe when a single instance runs.

Delay in seconds after which an instance that reset an index during a rolling deploy re-asserts the indexing cursor of that model, so a stale cursor written by an instance still running an older version does not skip rows. Must exceed the longest indexing round. Set to `0` to disable once every instance runs OpenAEV 3.261001.0 or later.
Maximum number of concurrent connections of the search engine client, applied both per route and in total; default `40`.
Maximum number of fields per index (`index.mapping.total_fields.limit`) set in the index templates OpenAEV creates; default `4096`.
Number of documents in a primary shard at which the lifecycle policy OpenAEV creates (ILM on Elasticsearch, ISM on OpenSearch) rolls an index over to a new one; default `75000000`.
Size of a primary shard at which the lifecycle policy OpenAEV creates (ILM on Elasticsearch, ISM on OpenSearch) rolls an index over to a new one; default `50Gb`.
Maximum `from + size` of a search on the indices OpenAEV creates (`index.max_result_window`), which bounds how deep results can be paged; default `100000`. Applies to new indices only.
Number of replica shards of each index OpenAEV creates in the search engine; default `1`. Applies to new indices only.
Number of primary shards of each index OpenAEV creates in the search engine; default `1`. Applies to new indices only.
Whether OpenAEV verifies the TLS certificate of the search engine against its trusted certificates; default `true`. Set to `false` to accept any certificate and host name, for a self-signed engine.
Maximum number of results a full-text search across all of OpenAEV's indices returns; default `500`.
How long, in milliseconds, the search engine client waits for a response (and for a free connection in its pool) before failing the request; default `60000`.

Log level of the HikariCP database connection pool; the platform ships `warn`, which keeps its connection leak warnings (connections held more than 30 seconds) visible.
Debug mode emits on io.openaev.debug at INFO/WARN; the parent io.openaev is pinned to ERROR, so the debug subtree is raised explicitly. Harmless when debug mode is off (those classes emit nothing).

Name pattern of the rotated files of Spring Boot's default log file appender; the platform ships `${LOG_FILE}.-%d{yyyy-MM-dd}.%i`, but OpenAEV's logging configuration writes its logs to the console and does not use that appender, so it has no effect.
Whether the Actuator health endpoint shows the details of each component; the platform ships `always`, but only the `prometheus` endpoint is exposed over HTTP.

Actuator: only the Prometheus scrape is exposed, and it is served on the API port, so it is rejected with a 401 unless openaev.metrics.key is set and sent as "Authorization: Bearer <key>". Empty key (the default) denies every actuator request. The management port follows server.port so the scrape stays on the port ActuatorSecurityConfig guards; a hardened deployment can point it at a dedicated, unpublished port instead.

Port on which OpenAEV serves the Actuator endpoints (the Prometheus scrape); the platform ships `${server.port}`, so the scrape stays behind the `openaev.metrics.key` check, and a hardened deployment can move it to a dedicated port that is not published.

Correlation ids: DebugTracingContextInitializer excludes the tracing auto-configuration unless debug mode is active, so no Tracer is created and no span/traceId is produced on any request, message or job path when off (management.tracing.enabled only gates export, not span creation). This sampling probability applies once tracing is active under debug mode.

Enterprise Edition license certificate (PEM) of the platform; when set, it takes precedence over the license entered in the settings. Empty by default: the license from the settings applies, if any.
Only reported in the anonymous usage telemetry, which lists the enabled authentication strategies; this version has no Kerberos login. `false` by default.

Commit the running build was made from, filled when the Docker image is built (`OPENAEV_COMMIT`); operators do not set it. Shown with the version in the platform information panel, hidden when empty.
Cookie validity sliding window (default 1 day). Each request re-issues the cookie with this Max-Age, so active users are never logged out by cookie expiration
Name of the browser cookie from which the platform reads a user's API token; the cookie is also deleted at logout. Default `openaev_token`.

Sender email address of all outgoing emails (the IMAP username is used instead when IMAP is enabled). It cannot be changed from the UI

Default Reply-To address used on outgoing emails
Reserved to development: leave it unset.

Local folder with extra trusted TLS certificates (public `.pem` files) to reach external applications such as CrowdStrike, Tanium or SentinelOne. Setting up the frontend url if frontend and backend are on a different server
Internal identifier of the platform configuration, `global` by default; operators do not set it, and no code of this version reads it.

Maximum size of the logs an implant sends back, passed as its `max_size` argument in the commands the executors run on endpoints. Default `1000000`; the unit is decided by the implant, not by the platform.

UUID of this platform instance, which platform-bound Enterprise Edition licenses must match. Empty: a random UUID is generated at the first start and kept in the database; when set, it must be a valid UUID and replaces the stored one at startup.
Path the browser is sent to after logout, appended to `openaev.frontend-url`. Default `/`.
URL of a map tile server for the dark theme, passed to the web interface in the platform settings; no screen of this version reads it. Empty by default.
URL of a map tile server for the light theme, passed to the web interface in the platform settings; no screen of this version reads it. Empty by default.
Application name, filled at build time from the project name; operators do not set it. Used as the Spring application name and in the footer of scheduled report emails (`OpenAEV` when empty).

Map of the RabbitMQ batching queues, one entry per queue (`inject-trace`, `workflows-ready`, `workflows-update`) with the settings below, declared for every tenant. Without `workflows-ready` or `workflows-update` the platform does not start; without `inject-trace`, execution traces are processed one by one as they arrive.
Startup run mode (`normal` or `safe`). In `safe`, Quartz background processing is disabled. See [Run modes](../../deployment/platform/run-modes.md).

When `true`, the session cookie dies when the browser closes (server-side timeout still applies). When `false`, users stay logged in across browser restarts: the cookie is re-issued on every request (sliding Max-Age), so it only expires after `openaev.cookie-duration` of inactivity

SameSite attribute of the session cookie: `None`, `Lax`, `Strict`, or blank to omit it. `Lax` drops the cookie on POST login callbacks (SAML2, OpenID `form_post`); `Strict` breaks all SSO (Single Sign-On) callbacks. `None` forces the `Secure` flag, for HTTPS SSO deployments
Idle time before the UI locks the screen and asks the user to continue or log out (0 = disabled, e.g. 30m). Must be lower than the session timeout
Turn on to accept self-signed or insecure SSL certificates
Platform version, filled at build time from the project version; operators do not set it. Shown in the platform information panel and in the API description.
Turn on for environments that use a proxy
Login email of the admin user (for example `admin@openaev.io`)
Key used with the salt to derive the 256-bit key that encrypts sensitive data in the database
Salt used with the encryption key. Must be at least 8 bytes long
API token of the admin user (must be a valid UUIDv4)
Max number of pending jobs per agent before marking it overloaded. 0 disables the check.
Above this many executions a simulation's graph is served collapsed by default. The bound is the front's render ceiling, not backend latency: a full graph larger than this is not renderable.
Beyond this many changed rows, a delta poll is answered with a resync instead: past that size assembling the delta costs more than a reload, which the client would do anyway to re-lay out.

Maximum size, in bytes, of the input or output of a change recorded in an audit log event; a larger one has its long strings cut, then keeps only key fields, then is replaced by a short preview. Default `32768`; `0` or less removes the cap.

Share of the maximum JVM heap in use (from `0` to `1`) at which audit events skip the full normalization and keep only the redaction rules and the size cap, when `skip-on-high-load` is on. Default `0.90`.
Process CPU load (from `0` to `1`) at which audit events skip the full normalization and keep only the redaction rules and the size cap, when `skip-on-high-load` is on. Default `0.90`.
Maximum size, in bytes, of a text value in an audit event that exceeds `max-event-size-bytes`; longer values are cut and end with `...[TRUNCATED]`. Default `1024`.
Turns off the normalization of audit events: inputs and outputs are recorded as they come, with no size cap, only the field redaction done beforehand still applies. Default `false`.

When `true` (default), audit events skip the full normalization while heap usage or process CPU load reaches `max-heap-usage-ratio` or `max-process-cpu-load`, keeping only the redaction rules and the size cap.
Length, in characters, of the serialized payload kept as `preview` when an audit event still exceeds `max-event-size-bytes` after truncation. Default `2048`.

Interval, in milliseconds, at which the platform processes the delayed workflow steps whose time has come. Default `10000`.
Production barrier: in production (no dev/test/ci profile) the mode refuses to start unless this separate override is also set. Turning openaev.debug.enabled on is not enough in production.
Auto-disable the verbose tracing after this duration (0 = never). A full removal of the datasource proxy still needs a restart.

Global, instance-wide debug mode. OFF by default. When off there is no datasource proxy on the query hot path, no parameter capture and no extra per-request allocation. Activate (ideally via env var OPENAEV_DEBUG_ENABLED=true) ONLY for diagnostics, never in steady production: a loud warning is logged repeatedly while it is on. See docs/docs/administration/debug-mode.md for the full reference and the writable volume needed in containers.

Group of the Java Flight Recorder settings of debug mode (`enabled`, `max-size`, `max-age`, `duration`, `settings`); a recording starts while `openaev.debug.enabled` is `true` and `openaev.debug.jfr.enabled` is `true`, its default.
Interval between two dumps of the debug JFR recording to a `.jfr` file in `openaev.debug.output-dir`, as a duration (at least one second). Default `10m`.
JFR recording (bounded in size and time, written to output-dir).
Maximum age of the events the debug JFR recording keeps, as a duration. Default `1h`.
Maximum on-disk size of the debug JFR recording, as a data size. Default `100MB`.
Built-in JFR profile of the debug recording: `profile` (default, richer, with a noticeable overhead) or `default` (lighter).

Group of the masking settings of debug output: `enabled` (`true` by default, keep it) hides secrets and personal data such as passwords, tokens and email addresses, and `mask-all-parameters` masks every SQL parameter value.
Masking of secrets and personal data. Keep enabled.
Deny-by-default: mask every parameter value (keep only column name + type). Opt-in to reveal less.

Group of the per-request ORM summary of debug mode, one log event per request to spot repeated queries; `summary-to-file`, `false` by default, writes it to a rotated file in `openaev.debug.output-dir` instead of the console.
Writable directory for debug artifacts: JFR recordings and the rotated SQL log file. On a read-only container, point this at a mounted writable volume.

Group of the SQL logging of debug mode: while `openaev.debug.enabled` is `true` and `enabled` is `true` (its default), every statement is written with its timing and masked parameters to the rotated file `openaev-debug-sql.log` in `openaev.debug.output-dir`. Set `slow-query-threshold` (for example `50ms`) to log only slower statements.
SQL statement logging (timing + masked parameters), written to a rotated file (openaev-debug-sql.log) in output-dir, off the console. Active only when debug mode is on.
0 logs every statement; set e.g. 50ms to only log slow ones.
How often the "debug mode is active" warning repeats.

Interval between two background connectivity probes of the dependencies (ISO-8601 duration). `/api/health` serves the result of the last probe and never contacts a dependency itself; it answers 503 once a required dependency (database, RabbitMQ, file storage) is down or has not been probed for 3 intervals
Key passed as `health_access_key` to the health check endpoint (`/api/health`). Change it in production

Interval between two background computations of the storage sizes returned by `/api/health?details=true` and exported as `openaev_storage_used_bytes` (ISO-8601 duration). Computing them walks the whole object storage listing and queries the engine cluster, so low values are costly
SMTP connection monitoring, enabled by default. Allow you to monitor service state from healthchecks and settings page

IMAP sent directory to synchronize from

Tables filtered by marking clearance (statement inspector + is_marking_set_allowed). A table is eligible once it has a `marking_ids text[]` column; listing it here turns the filtering on - but only once the MARKING preview feature is also enabled via openaev.enabled-dev-features (see above). Empty means the marking dimension is inert and the emitted SQL is unchanged. Only tables carrying markings are listed: the tables derived from them (findings, injects_expectations... see MarkingDerivedTables) are filtered with them, and are not listed.
Scrape key for `/actuator/prometheus`, sent by the scraper as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. While empty (the default), every `/actuator/**` request is rejected with a 401
Delay in seconds before processing the SIMULATION_COMPLETED notification event (default: 3600 = 1h, allows expectations to be scored first)
Turn on to let webhook notifiers call internal or private addresses. This skips the SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) check on private addresses; scheme, host and HTTP verb checks still apply
Number of days notification events are kept, in every tenant, before the purge deletes them. Default `35`.
Value of the `audience` parameter added to the authorization request sent to this OpenID provider. Empty adds none.
Name of the SAML attribute that holds the user's first name for this SAML2 provider, copied to the user at each login. OpenID providers use the `given_name` claim instead.

JSON list of group mappings for this provider, each with `idpGroup`, `userGroup`, `autoCreate` and an optional `tenantId`: at each login the user joins the mapped groups found in their `groups_path` attributes and leaves the mapped groups no longer there. Empty maps no group.
Name of the SAML attribute that holds the user's last name for this SAML2 provider, copied to the user at each login. OpenID providers use the `family_name` claim instead.

Comma-separated roles that make a user a platform administrator when one of them is found in the `roles_path` attributes; when set, the administrator status is granted or removed at each login. Empty creates new users as non-administrators and leaves existing users unchanged.
Comma-separated names of the attributes (SAML) or claims (OpenID) of this provider from which the platform reads the user's roles, compared with `roles_admin`. Empty reads no role.

Tenant a user signing in through this provider is attached to, with that tenant's auto-assign groups, the first time. Empty uses the default tenant; an id missing from the database is logged and ignored.
Number of RabbitMQ channels consuming the queue that batches the execution traces implants and injectors send back. `8` in the shipped file, `1` when the entry omits it.

Prefetch count of each consumer channel of the queue that batches the execution traces implants and injectors send back: how many messages RabbitMQ hands over before they are acknowledged. `1000` in the shipped file, `30` when the entry omits it.

Batch threshold of the queue that batches the execution traces implants and injectors send back: once more than this many messages are buffered for one worker, the batch is processed at once, without waiting for `worker-frequency`. `200` in the shipped file, `100` when the entry omits it.
Number of RabbitMQ channels publishing to the queue that batches the execution traces implants and injectors send back. `2` in the shipped file, `1` when the entry omits it.

Prefetch count set on each publishing channel of the queue that batches the execution traces implants and injectors send back; `0`, the shipped value, means no limit, and `30` applies when the entry omits it.

Name of the queue that batches the execution traces implants and injectors send back in RabbitMQ: the platform declares the queue `<rabbitmq prefix>-<tenant id>_execution_<name>` and its exchange from it. `inject-trace` in the shipped file.

Interval, in milliseconds, at which the buffered messages of the queue that batches the execution traces implants and injectors send back are processed even when the batch is not full. Default `10000`.

Number of worker threads processing the batches of the queue that batches the execution traces implants and injectors send back; messages are spread across workers by their key. `8` in the shipped file, `1` when the entry omits it.
Number of RabbitMQ channels consuming the queue of workflow steps ready to run. `1` in the shipped file, `1` when the entry omits it.

Prefetch count of each consumer channel of the queue of workflow steps ready to run: how many messages RabbitMQ hands over before they are acknowledged. `1000` in the shipped file, `30` when the entry omits it.

Batch threshold of the queue of workflow steps ready to run: once more than this many messages are buffered for one worker, the batch is processed at once, without waiting for `worker-frequency`. `200` in the shipped file, `100` when the entry omits it.
Number of RabbitMQ channels publishing to the queue of workflow steps ready to run. `1` in the shipped file, `1` when the entry omits it.
Prefetch count set on each publishing channel of the queue of workflow steps ready to run; `0`, the shipped value, means no limit, and `30` applies when the entry omits it.

Name of the queue of workflow steps ready to run in RabbitMQ: the platform declares the queue `<rabbitmq prefix>-<tenant id>_execution_<name>` and its exchange from it. `workflows-ready` in the shipped file.
Interval, in milliseconds, at which the buffered messages of the queue of workflow steps ready to run are processed even when the batch is not full. Default `10000`.
Number of worker threads processing the batches of the queue of workflow steps ready to run; messages are spread across workers by their key. `1` in the shipped file, `1` when the entry omits it.
Number of RabbitMQ channels consuming the queue of update events (new trace, new output) of running workflow steps. `1` in the shipped file, `1` when the entry omits it.

Prefetch count of each consumer channel of the queue of update events (new trace, new output) of running workflow steps: how many messages RabbitMQ hands over before they are acknowledged. `1000` in the shipped file, `30` when the entry omits it.

Batch threshold of the queue of update events (new trace, new output) of running workflow steps: once more than this many messages are buffered for one worker, the batch is processed at once, without waiting for `worker-frequency`. `200` in the shipped file, `100` when the entry omits it.
Number of RabbitMQ channels publishing to the queue of update events (new trace, new output) of running workflow steps. `1` in the shipped file, `1` when the entry omits it.

Prefetch count set on each publishing channel of the queue of update events (new trace, new output) of running workflow steps; `0`, the shipped value, means no limit, and `30` applies when the entry omits it.

Name of the queue of update events (new trace, new output) of running workflow steps in RabbitMQ: the platform declares the queue `<rabbitmq prefix>-<tenant id>_execution_<name>` and its exchange from it. `workflows-update` in the shipped file.

Interval, in milliseconds, at which the buffered messages of the queue of update events (new trace, new output) of running workflow steps are processed even when the batch is not full. Default `10000`.

Number of worker threads processing the batches of the queue of update events (new trace, new output) of running workflow steps; messages are spread across workers by their key. `1` in the shipped file, `1` when the entry omits it.
Whether or not the calls to the management plugin of rabbitmq can be insecure
Management port of the RabbitMQ Server
Hard cap in milliseconds on a single publish, so a broker that stops answering cannot hold a database transaction open. Must be strictly positive, otherwise the default applies.
Path to the p12 trust store (for example `file:/path/to/truststore.p12`) with the CA of the RabbitMQ server certificate. Used when SSL is on. When empty, the JVM default trust store applies.

Spelling of the shipped file for the trust store used for TLS to RabbitMQ (`openaev.rabbitmq.ssl`); the code reads `openaev.rabbitmq.trust-store`, so this spelling is ignored and the JVM default trust store applies.
Maximum requests per second for authenticated requests, segmented per user account.
Maximum requests per second for unauthenticated requests, segmented per originating IP address.
Turn on to enable global rate limiting on the REST API
Rate limit bucket store backend. Only `IN_MEMORY` is available.
Maximum number of simultaneous browser contexts. Bounds Chromium memory usage
URL the headless browser uses to reach the platform. Empty uses loopback (`http(s)://localhost:{server.port}`). Override only when loopback does not serve the UI
Maximum duration of a single render, in seconds
Number of days to keep execution traces (one row per agent execution message). `0` disables the purge job

Use the AWS IAM role of the host, through AWS STS (Security Token Service), instead of access keys
Grace period in minutes after the start time of a time-based Inject, during which it can still run. Past this period, the Inject is set in error. Values below `1` are treated as `1`.
StarterPack feature, providing default endpoint, asset group, scenarios and dashboards

Database tables whose tenant isolation the database itself enforces, on every statement. Each release ships the list its code needs: leave it as shipped and do not override it. A table left out can lose its tenant isolation, and naming a table that isolates itself stops the platform at startup.
Reserved to development: leave it unset.

Turn on to let theme logo and image URLs point at internal or private addresses, for on-premise networks with no public place to host a logo. This skips the SSRF (Server-Side Request Forgery) check on private addresses, both when the theme is saved and when reports are rendered, where it applies to every external resource the renderer loads. The URL must still use `https` and have a host
Number of days added after an exercise end date before URL access tokens expire
Number of days to retain expired or revoked URL access tokens before the purge job deletes them
Makes the built-in email injector contracts available to XLS import mappers. `true` in the shipped file; the key has no default, so the platform does not start without it.
Makes the built-in SMS (OVH) injector contract available to XLS import mappers. `true` in the shipped file; the key has no default, so the platform does not start without it.
Interval in seconds at which the connectivity with XTM Hub is checked
Enables the XTM Hub connectivity collector
Identifier of the XTM Hub connectivity collector

Interval, in seconds, between two syncs of the XTM Hub news feed, counted from the end of the previous run, when `openaev.xtm.hub.collector.enable` is `true`. Default `3600`; `0` or less falls back to it.
Emails the platform or tenant administrators when the connection to XTM Hub has been lost for more than 24 hours. `true` by default.
When specified, override `openaev.xtm.hub.url` during backend calls
XTM One registration token. With the URL, OpenAEV registers with XTM One every 5 minutes
XTM One URL, as reachable from OpenAEV (an internal address such as `http://xtm-one:4000` in Docker works)

GraphQL API URL of the OpenCTI platform of the default tenant, when it is not `url` followed by `/graphql`. The code reads it as `api-url`: under the `api_url` spelling of the shipped file it is not matched and the default URL applies.

Connects the default tenant (one entry per tenant id) to OpenCTI: with `url` and `token` set, the platform registers its security coverage connector there and keeps it alive. `false` in the shipped file.
API token the platform uses to authenticate to the OpenCTI platform of the default tenant; required for the connection to be made.
URL of the OpenCTI platform of the default tenant, also shown in the tenant settings; its GraphQL API is reached at this URL followed by `/graphql`.

Read once, at the first startup that migrates the injector settings into the integration catalog: when `true`, OpenAEV creates and starts an OVHCloud SMS injector from the `ovh.sms.*` keys; when `false`, it creates none. Changing it afterwards has no effect, and the injector is then deployed from the catalog.
ID of the builtin Ovh injector
Name of the builtin Ovh injector

Whether OpenAEV starts the Pyroscope continuous profiling agent at startup and labels profiles with the REST endpoint or background job being run; the platform ships `false`. While it is on, debug mode does not start its own JFR recording.
Application name under which OpenAEV sends its profiles to the Pyroscope server; default `OpenAEV`.
Timeout for uploading a profile to the Pyroscope server, as a duration; the platform ships `300s`.
Allocation profiling threshold of the Pyroscope agent, in bytes allocated between two samples; the platform ships `512k`, and an empty value disables allocation profiling.
Event the Pyroscope agent samples for CPU profiling (`itimer`, `cpu`, `wall`, `ctimer`...); default `itimer`.
Lock contention threshold of the Pyroscope agent: lock waits longer than this are recorded; the platform ships `10ms`, and an empty value disables lock profiling.
URL of the Pyroscope server OpenAEV sends its profiles to when the agent is enabled; the platform ships the placeholder `<pyroscope.url>`, and the code defaults to `http://localhost:4040`.
Maximum number of attempts OpenAEV makes when the AI remediation webservice (`remediation.detection.webservice`) answers an HTTP error; after the last one, the request fails. Unset, `3`.
Time in milliseconds OpenAEV waits before calling the AI remediation webservice again after an HTTP error. Unset, `30000`; `0` or less retries at once.
Whether the web server compresses its HTTP responses (gzip) for clients that accept it; the platform ships `true`.
How OpenAEV honors the `X-Forwarded-*` and `Forwarded` headers set by a reverse proxy when it builds redirect and callback URLs; the platform ships `framework`, which applies them in Spring.
Whether the web server accepts HTTP/2; the platform ships `true`, over TLS when `server.ssl.enabled` is on and in cleartext (h2c) otherwise.
Path under which OpenAEV serves its web interface and API; the platform ships `/`. The frontend and the report renderer follow it, so set it when a reverse proxy publishes OpenAEV under a sub-path.
Character set of HTTP requests and responses; the platform ships `UTF-8`.
Rolling session timeout: every request extends the session by this duration. Sessions are persisted in PostgreSQL and survive platform restarts
Turn on to enable SSL on the local server
Character set the web server uses to decode request URLs; the platform ships `UTF-8`.
Name of the application; the platform ships `${openaev.name}`, the platform name.
Base path of the repository endpoints Spring Data REST would expose; the platform ships `/api`, the path under which OpenAEV's own REST API is served.
Connection property HikariCP passes to the JDBC driver; the platform ships `true`, but it is a MySQL driver setting that the PostgreSQL driver does not read.
Connection property HikariCP passes to the JDBC driver; the platform ships `250`, but it is a MySQL driver setting that the PostgreSQL driver does not read.
Connection property HikariCP passes to the JDBC driver; the platform ships `2048`, but it is a MySQL driver setting that the PostgreSQL driver does not read.
Connection property HikariCP passes to the JDBC driver; the platform ships `true`, but it is a MySQL driver setting that the PostgreSQL driver does not read.

Log the acquisition stack trace of any thread holding a connection for more than 30s ("Apparent connection leak detected", WARN on com.zaxxer.hikari ? visible with production log levels). Together with io.openaev.diagnostics.PoolExhaustionWatchdog (ERROR + thread dump on sustained saturation), this names the code paths pinning connections whenever the pool gets exhausted. The connection is NOT killed: legit long holders (bulk indexing, migrations) just log evidence.
Maximum number of database connections in the pool
Whether Flyway baselines a non-empty database that has no migration history table before migrating it; the platform ships `true`.
Version Flyway records when it baselines an existing database; the platform ships `0`, so every OpenAEV migration still runs.

Ignore applied migrations that are no longer resolved locally (e.g. the 20260720 migrations renumbered in #6808): instances that already ran the old version numbers must not fail validation on boot. The renumbered replacements are idempotent.
Where Flyway finds the database migrations OpenAEV applies at startup; the platform ships `classpath:io/openaev/migration`, the migrations bundled with the platform, and it should not be changed.
optionally enable out of order processing. this allows for easier development by avoiding migrations clashes https://github.com/OpenAEV-Platform/openaev/issues/5281
Password of the PostgreSQL account Flyway uses to migrate the database schema at startup; the platform ships `${spring.datasource.password}`, the password of the main datasource.
Whether Flyway takes a transaction-level advisory lock on PostgreSQL while migrating; the platform ships `false`, so Flyway uses a session-level lock instead.
Name of the table in which Flyway records the migrations already applied; the platform ships `migrations`.
JDBC URL of the PostgreSQL database Flyway migrates at startup; the platform ships `${spring.datasource.url}`, the main datasource.
PostgreSQL account Flyway uses to migrate the database schema at startup; the platform ships `${spring.datasource.username}`, the account of the main datasource.
Character set of the templates rendered through Spring Boot's FreeMarker support; the platform ships `UTF-8`.
Whether Hibernate creates or alters the database schema at startup; the platform ships `none`, because the Flyway migrations manage the schema.
Batch lazy/eager association loading (IN (?, ?, ...) instead of one SELECT per entity). The model has many EAGER collections without @Fetch(SUBSELECT); this caps the N+1 cost.
Number of statements Hibernate groups into one JDBC batch when it writes to PostgreSQL; the platform ships `30`.
Whether Hibernate orders inserts by entity so that they can be sent in JDBC batches; the platform ships `true`.
Whether Hibernate orders updates by entity so that they can be sent in JDBC batches; the platform ships `true`.
Character set of the emails OpenAEV sends through its SMTP server, such as the email injects; the platform ships `UTF-8`.
Character set of Spring message bundles; the platform ships `UTF-8`.
Strategy Spring MVC uses to match request paths to the API routes; the platform ships `ant_path_matcher`.
Name of the Quartz scheduler that runs OpenAEV's background jobs; the platform ships `OpenAEV_Scheduler`.
Number of threads of the Quartz scheduler that runs OpenAEV's background jobs, hence how many jobs run at the same time; the platform ships `10`.
Issuer URL of the OpenID Connect provider of this registration; OpenAEV discovers the provider's endpoints and keys from it.
Client ID OpenAEV presents to the OpenID Connect provider of this registration.

Display name of this OpenID Connect registration in Spring Security; the OpenAEV login button does not show it, it shows `openaev.provider.<registrationId>.login`, or `Login with <registrationId>` when that is unset.
Client secret that authenticates OpenAEV to the OpenID Connect provider of this registration.

URL the OpenID Connect provider of this registration sends users back to after they sign in, normally `${openaev.base-url}/login/oauth2/code/<registrationId>`; it must match the redirect URL declared at the provider.
Comma-separated scopes OpenAEV requests from the OpenID Connect provider of this registration, for example `openid,profile,email`.
URL or location of the SAML 2 metadata of the identity provider of this registration, from which OpenAEV reads its sign-in URL and signing certificates.
Entity ID by which OpenAEV identifies itself to the SAML 2 identity provider of this registration; it must match the service provider declared at the identity provider.
Maximum size of one file uploaded to OpenAEV; the platform ships `5GB`.
Maximum size of one upload request to OpenAEV, all files included; the platform ships `5GB`.
Built-in cleanup is disabled: the SessionManager audit-aware cleanup job replaces it.
Session tables are created by a Flyway migration, never by Spring Session itself.

Idle timeout of the user sessions stored in PostgreSQL: every authenticated request extends the session by this duration; the platform ships `${server.servlet.session.timeout}`, so it follows that key (`1440m`, 24 hours).
Path at which OpenAEV serves the OpenAPI description of its REST API; the platform ships `/api-docs`.
